title: Connecticut POSTC General Notice 25-05 — further waiver of citizenship requirement
summary: Primary Connecticut POSTC notice documenting the 2020 lawful-permanent-resident waiver and the March 13, 2025 extension of police probationary-candidate eligibility to DACA recipients.

evidence.claim: POSTC states that RCSA § 7-294e-16(c) contains a U.S.-citizenship condition for probationary police candidates and that POSTC may waive regulations under CGS § 7-294d(a)(20).

POSTC states that at its November 19, 2020 special meeting it partially waived the citizenship requirement to extend eligibility to permanent legal residents, and that this waiver was reflected in the POSTC-51 form.

POSTC states that at its March 13, 2025 meeting it further waived the citizenship requirement to extend eligibility to DACA recipients in addition to permanent legal residents, and updated POSTC-51 accordingly.

caveats: The notice changes the POSTC eligibility floor through waivers; it does not by itself prove the final wording, effective date, or roll-call details of Danbury's September 2026 ordinance amendment.

title: Danbury PD applicant eligibility — POSTC waiver alignment
summary: Authoritative POSTC notice resolves the statewide eligibility bridge behind Danbury's 2026 amendment: LPR eligibility dates to the November 2020 waiver and DACA eligibility to the March 13, 2025 further waiver; Danbury's final primary September record remains unpublished in the official Agenda Center at collection time.

caveats: POSTC General Notice 25-05 establishes statewide waiver history and eligibility, not the final Danbury enactment text.
The official Danbury Agenda Center still does not publish September 1 minutes at collection time, so the exact primary roll call and any final textual amendments remain unresolved.
No individual's citizenship, immigration status, or eligibility is inferred from these policy records.

findings: POSTC General Notice 25-05 is the authoritative state record tying lawful-permanent-resident eligibility to POSTC's November 19, 2020 partial waiver and DACA-recipient eligibility to its March 13, 2025 further waiver.
The notice identifies the waiver authority as CGS § 7-294d(a)(20) and the underlying citizenship regulation as RCSA § 7-294e-16(c), and says POSTC-51 was updated to reflect the eligibility change.
Danbury's previously captured proposal-stage section 22-27(a) language therefore has a concrete state-policy alignment surface rather than merely a media-described rationale.

As of September 15, 2026 the official Danbury City Council Agenda Center exposes the September 1 agenda but no minutes or media link, so the final adopted wording, named 18-2 roll call, effective date, and formal enactment identifier remain primary-record gaps.
conclusions: Issue #2514 can now distinguish statewide POSTC eligibility from Danbury's local ordinance: POSTC permits probationary-candidate eligibility for U.S. citizens, permanent legal residents, and DACA recipients through the cited waivers, while Danbury's local code amendment removes its stricter local citizenship barrier.

The policy change expands who may be considered; these records do not establish that any specific applicant or officer belongs to any immigration-status category, nor do they waive unrelated background, training, certification, or appointment requirements.
counterarguments: Published regulations can still display the older citizenship text even though POSTC exercised waiver authority; General Notice 25-05 explicitly documents that waiver mechanism and should not be collapsed into a claim that the regulation text itself was repealed.

Secondary reporting describes an 18-2 September 1 vote, but until the City's final minutes/adopted instrument are published that roll call and final text should remain source-qualified rather than promoted to primary-record fact.
unresolved: September 1, 2026 final City Council minutes and named roll call, including the two NO votes.

title: Research pass: Danbury PD POSTC eligibility alignment (2026-09-15)
summary: Bounded Worker 2 continuation that resolves the authoritative Connecticut POSTC citizenship-waiver lineage behind Danbury's amendment and records the current absence of September 1 minutes from the City's public Agenda Center.

provenance.method: corpus-first bounded primary-source reconciliation for issue #2514

data.research_question: What authoritative state record governs lawful-permanent-resident and DACA eligibility for Connecticut police appointments, how does it relate to Danbury's 2026 amendment, and has Danbury published the final September 1 primary record yet?
data.method: Searched the existing Auto-Dig corpus first, then reviewed Connecticut POSTC General Notice 25-05 and the current official Danbury City Council Agenda Center. Reused existing May 2026 Danbury proposal evidence instead of duplicating it and preserved the absence of September minutes only as a time-bounded publication-state observation.
classification_rules: POSTC waiver authority and local ordinance enactment are modeled as separate legal/policy layers.
A current missing minutes link is a publication-state observation, not proof that minutes do not exist.
No person's citizenship or immigration status is inferred.
Proposal text and secondary reports are not promoted to final primary enactment state without the adopted instrument or final minutes.

findings.finding: General Notice 25-05 resolves the statewide waiver sequence: permanent legal residents became eligible through the November 19, 2020 partial waiver; DACA recipients were added through the March 13, 2025 further waiver.

The September 1, 2026 Danbury City Council meeting still has no public minutes or media link in the official Agenda Center at collection time, leaving the final local enactment/roll-call record unresolved.
